requirements.requirement: Serve an APT package repository from local storage on node1.
requirements.summary: Repository metadata and the package artifact were present under /srv/local-apt-repository. The enabled service listened on port 8080 and returned the Packages index successfully, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the usual remote repositories unreachable while the local repository remains usable.
requirements.summary: APT's ordinary Ubuntu archive and security requests failed through the deliberately unreachable proxy, while it downloaded the local index and selected local-repo-proof 1.0.0 from node1:8080.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while the remote repositories are unreachable.
requirements.summary: APT fetched local-repo-proof 1.0.0 from node1:8080, dpkg reported it installed, and its executable and origin file produced the expected output. The installation and payload remained healthy after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Node1 served a local APT repository, remote Ubuntu repositories were demonstrably unreachable, and APT installed and executed a package fetched from the local service. Restart evidence is complete and agrees with the lifecycle boot-identity observations.
limitations: The post-reboot reinstall did not independently demonstrate another repository download because APT reported 0 bytes to fetch; the original installation nevertheless directly recorded the package being fetched from node1:8080.
Lifecycle snapshots are bounded inventories and do not independently enumerate every repository, APT, or systemd configuration file; those details rely on the captured executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive setup mutations had clear task roles, and the final system had healthy dpkg state and no failed services. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered repository, artifact, package, and system state. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred: the already verified package was reinstalled after recovery, without adding proof of a repository fetch because APT used its cached archive; it retained the same package version rather than being explicitly reverted (cmd-6297e863733342bb). The final evidence probe also left /tmp/repo-post-packages behind (cmd-3c6a3090c4d444e6). Minor security concerns remain from trusting an unsigned HTTP repository and exposing its simple HTTP server on all interfaces, although both changes directly supported the requested repository workflow.
